title: Quiet-band release scheduling and notelets
body:
Overview:

This doc is a working sketch for a low-signal "quiet-band" release pattern: small changes are released into a stable subset of traffic during low-activity windows to limit blast radius while exercising rollout automation and telemetry gates. Goal is predictable, low-risk incrementals (config flips, nonblocking feature flags, small model variant swaps) that we can ship with minimal oncall churn.

Primary goals:
- Validate routing, sampling, and partition-aware caches end-to-end.
- Catch regressions in metrics sensitive to tail latency and error-rate without affecting majority of users.
- Exercise rollback automation and operator runbook (fast cut-to-fallback).
- Produce release notes draft and post-release signal digest for product/CS.

Scope (what belongs in quiet-band):
- Non-breaking API changes behind flags
- Model variant swaps with compatible tokenizer/outputs
- Small infra tweaks (autoscaler config, cache TTLs)
- Observability or logging format changes (non-consumer-facing)

Out-of-scope (do not include):
- Breaking schema migrations
- Large model upgrades or dataset additions
- Changes requiring database migrations

10-day rollout calendar (template - adjust per release):
- D-7 (prep): create release branch, add banner to release-ops Slack, update Confluence note. Confirm owner and fallback model/route ids.
- D-6 (merge window one): land PRs, run CI smoke (unit + integration), tag release candidate.
- D-5 (canary dry run): local staging smoke with 100% synthetic traffic and KV-cache warmup scenario. Collect baseline traces.
- D-4 (quiet-band deploy 1): release to partition A (0.5% traffic) during 0100-0300 PST. Monitor 2x baseline for 60m.
- D-3 (quiet-band expand): if no gate trips, expand to partition B (1.5% total). Run end-to-end chat and embeddings smoke queries.
- D-2 (telemetry soak): keep at partition B for 48h; collect p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, cost-per-token.
- D-1 (preflight): finalize release notes draft, mark release in calendar, schedule 1h watch with SRE + owner.
- D0 (broad ramp): if metrics stable, schedule ramp window with step increases (5% -> 20% -> 50%) over an 8h quiet window.
- D+1 (stabilize): observe for 24h at target percentage; run extended integration test.
- D+3 (postmortem): collect signal digest, finalize release notes, capture regressions and TODOs.

Preflight checklist (must be green before D-4):
- Owners assigned (owner, backup, SRE responder)
- Release branch cut and PRs LGTM
- Smoke test script updated for this release (idempotent queries)
- Rollback variant / route documented and validated in staging
- Alerts and dashboards annotated (links + expected thresholds)
- Token/credential rotations validated (if any changed)
- Deployment automation runbook review (steps, timeouts, helmsman commands)
- Communication plan: Slack notice + standup sync + Pager duty watch assigned

Day-of (quiet-band deploy 1) quick checklist:
- Confirm quiet window (timezone) with oncall
- Snapshot current traffic routing and snapshot model IDs
- Run pre-deploy smoke in canary infra (synthetic queries)
- Deploy to partition A (0.5%) using traffic-partition API
- Start 60m intensive monitoring (SLO dashboards, error logs, traces)
- If gate triggers: trigger rollback automation OR manual rollback (owner)
- If stable: post short status to Slack with metrics

Telemetry gates (automated + human):
- Auto gates (automated rollback triggers):
  - error-rate increase > 150% over baseline for 5m
  - p99 latency > baseline + 250ms for 5m
  - spike in 5xx or infra OOMs (any occurrence)
- Human gates (require human confirmation):
  - cost-per-token change > 25% (requires product sign-off)
  - unexpected change in model output quality (NLP eval drop on quickset)

Rollback criteria and procedure:
- If auto-gate triggers: traffic-partition engine reverts to previous variant and notifies owner + SRE. Owner runs quick validation checklist.
- Manual rollback: owner runs rollback playbook (helm rollback OR change route to fallback route id), validate health, escalate to oncall if not recovered in 10 minutes.
- Post-rollback: capture snapshots (logs, traces, heap profiles) and open an incident ticket for triage.

Operator notes (practical gotchas):
- Partitioning may leave stale KV cache state; clear only for affected shards to avoid mass cache churn.
- If a rollback partially applied (some shards reverted), run convergence check (expected model ID per shard).
- Be mindful of billing attribution when running synthetic load during quiet hours.
- If skyline spike seen in tracing, attach trace ids to ticket and pin examples in release notes.

Release notes draft (to be copied into product/marketing once final):
- Feature: "Adaptive prefix caching tuning" - reduces average token compute by ~6% in experiments (internal flag behind quiet-band). JIRA-3412.
- Fix: "Auth header parsing edge-case" - intermittent 401 on long-lived sessions resolved. PR#4721.
- Infra: "Autoscaler soft-start" - smoother ramp behavior for dedicated pools; reduces ramp thundering observed in bench runs.
- Known issues: small subset of legacy clients may see increased p95 latency for early responses; mitigation: suggest client-side retry backoff.

Post-release digest template (fill in D+1 / D+3):
- Rollout summary: partition progression and times
- Signals observed: p50/p95/p99 latency delta, error-rate, 5xx counts, cost delta
- Actions taken: rollbacks, mitigations, config tweaks
- Follow-ups: list of tickets (owners, ETA)
- Communication: links to Slack thread, customer impact (if any), product bullet points for release notes

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Do we want a standard "quiet-band smoke-set" repo with curated queries? (yes -> owner: Marco)
- Add automated sanity check that validates tokenizer compatibility across model variants before routing (owner: Priya)
- Run a rehearsed rollback drill with SRE in the next ops sprint (owner: Jonah)
- Decide whether cost-per-token should be an automated gate or human-gated (engineering + product discussion)

Short checklist for finalization before marking "final":
- Fill in real metrics baselines in this doc
- Link to final PRs and release artifacts
- Get product sign-off on release notes
- Convert this sketch into a canned runbook in the Runbooks repo

Notes to self: rough, keep simple; prioritize safety and quick observability turn-around.

-- end --
